reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: The trial achieved fluorescent visualization of lymphatic drainage, indicating the fluorescein successfully reached and engaged lymphatic vessels as intended. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The fluorescent tracer mechanism worked as designed - lymphatic drainage was visualized, confirming the biological pathway was modulated. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite successful target engagement and pathway modulation, the primary endpoint failed. The agreement between fluorescein and standard technetium-99m tracer for sentinel lymph node detection was only 69.7%, which was below the threshold for clinical utility. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses were reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This appears to be a diagnostic accuracy study comparing two tracers. The failure suggests the fluorescent approach, while biologically active, was not sufficiently accurate compared to the gold standard radioactive tracer for clinical adoption.
